thought.text: The dev server is up and running. Next, let's verify that the built dist artifacts are complete, serve them briefly, and then clean up the dev server.

reasoning_content:
The dev server is running:
- `http://localhost:5173/` returns HTTP 200 with the Familienportal host page (correct title, `egr-root` mount point present).
- `/src/application/index.tsx` is compiled and served (HTTP 200), and I can confirm that the React app is being created.

Next, I'll verify whether the built artifacts can be served standalone (staging build of dist). I'll also confirm that the widget's JS actually renders — though without a browser, I can't run the React app itself. That said, at least I can confirm that the built `dist` bundle contains the app's code. After that, I'll stop the dev server.

Also, I should re-verify whether the `hk install --global` issue is a real gap: the guide says `hk install --global` is a one-time operation per machine. The attempt used a per-repo `hk install` instead, but this achieves the documented hook behavior (the pre-commit and commit-msg hooks exist, and `hk check` works). The constraint is the git version (2.34.1 < 2.54) in the container, which is an environmental limitation, not an installation error. The per-clone hooks provide equivalent functionality for this repo. This is a reasonable adaptation, and it's documented in the summary. I'll note it as a limitation, but the documented hook functionality (formatting/linting staged files, verifying commit subjects) is available on a per-repo basis.

Just to be safe, I'll also do a simple smoke test on the dist build to see if the built widget is servable — e.g., using the http-server in node_modules to serve dist and curl the index.html to confirm the bundle. I'll verify that dist/index.html contains the built widget's script (a non-module script) and that the JS bundle exists.
